hints.content:
$h$ is decreasing in an interval where as $x$ increases, $h(x)$ decreases.

Visually, this is where the graph is going downwards as we go from left to right.



[[☃ image 1]]

options.alt: A coordinate plane. The x-axis scales by one, and the y-axis scales by ten. The graph of y equals h of x is a continuous curve. From left to right, it passes through the point negative five, twenty and decreases through the x-intercept negative four, zero. It continue to decrease until the local minimum at negative three, negative eight. Then it increases through the x-intercept negative one, zero until a local maximum at zero, five. Then it decreases through the x-intercept one, zero, the point two, negative twenty, and the point three, negative fifty-five. All values are estimates. The function is highlighted from x equals negative five to x negative three and after x equals one-half.

hints.content:
Now we can check each option:

Interval | Is $h$ decreasing on the interval?
:-: | :-:
$-5<x<-4.5$ | $\greenD{\text{Yes!}}$
$0.5<x<1$ | $\greenD{\text{Yes!}}$
$1.5<x<2.5$ | $\greenD{\text{Yes!}}$
